analysis.title: Construction & Rental Equipment: September Dodge Construction Starts and the latest mega project starts
key_insights: Sep non-residential construction starts fell about 5% Y/Y in square footage, an improvement from about a 15% decline in Aug. Total non-resi square footage is still negative, but breadth improved.

The share of non-resi end markets with positive square-footage growth rose from about 45% in Aug to about 70% in Sep, above the historical median of about 55%. By value the share rebounded to 45%, below the historical median of 60%.

Warehouses fell about 15% Y/Y and parking about 30% Y/Y in Sep square footage. Office and bank buildings (which include data centers) rose about 20% and schools about 40% Y/Y in the note's summary figures.
Data centers are now about 30% of trailing-twelve-month mega-project starts, ahead of LNG at about 23%. They are the largest source of mega-project activity.
Mega projects were about 20% of Sep starts, totaling $15B (+about 25% Y/Y). Data centers, LNG and public infrastructure together made up roughly two-thirds of TTM mega-project activity.
The largest recent projects were the South Valley Data Center in Nevada (about $4.6B) and the Beacon Point Data Center in Texas (about $4.3B).
Bernstein says the slower decline and better breadth should support machinery, rental and infrastructure-exposed names: CAT, URI, SUNB, PWR and ETN.
Sep total starts by value were $111.3B, +1% Y/Y. TTM total starts value is $1,424.8B, +14% Y/Y, and TTM non-resi building plus non-building is +21% Y/Y.
Power plants, gas and communications starts rose 82% Y/Y in Sep to $11.3B. TTM for that category is $178.2B, +91% Y/Y.
Non-resi building starts by value rose 16% Y/Y in Sep to $49.7B. Office and bank buildings were $18.7B, +69% Y/Y. TTM office and bank value is $207.3B, +104% Y/Y.

Residential starts fell 5% Y/Y in square footage and 6% in value in Sep. Apartments were -20% in square footage and one-family houses were flat. Housing affordability declined in the latest read and remains well below pre-pandemic levels.
Bernstein's developer-profit-margin model, which leads non-resi starts by about 18 months, suggests non-resi square-footage starts will keep declining through at least the next 12 months.
Dollar value of starts has increasingly been driven by price inflation. Non-resi price per square foot rose 23% Y/Y in Sep to $495, while TTM non-resi square footage is -6% Y/Y.

For Arkema (Market-Perform), Bernstein reads the Sep starts as mixed to negative. Residential starts fell 3% in value, and non-resi value rose 16%, driven by office and bank buildings (+104%), which include data centers. Data centers are a very small opportunity for Arkema, with about €100m of targeted sales by 2030 (1% of 2025 sales).

sector_views.rationale: Non-resi decline is slowing and breadth is improving, which supports machinery, rental and infrastructure-exposed names. The developer-margin model still points to declining non-resi starts for at least 12 months.
Data centers are now the largest source of mega-project starts at about 30% of TTM, and office and bank buildings (which include data centers) are the main growth category.
Warehouse starts fell about 15% Y/Y and parking about 30% Y/Y in Sep square footage, the main drag on non-resi volumes.
Residential starts fell 5% Y/Y in square footage in Sep, and housing affordability remains well below pre-pandemic levels.

earnings_insights: CNH estimates in the ticker table are reported EPS: $0.55 (2025A) / $0.44 (2026E) / $0.60 (2027E). TTAM and LGN estimates are EBITDA in millions, and their valuations are EV/EBITDA.
Arkema adjusted EPS (EUR): 4.32 (2025A) / 4.64 (2026E) / 5.31 (2027E). Bernstein notes data center exposure is about €100m of targeted sales by 2030, 1% of 2025 sales.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The decline slowed from about -15% in Aug, but TTM square footage remains negative at -6% Y/Y.
Value is held up by price inflation and mega projects while volume in square feet is down.
Residential weakness is led by apartments (-20%). Bernstein notes non-resi usually lags resi by about 9 months.
Mega projects are concentrated in AI infrastructure.
Dollar value of starts is increasingly price-driven rather than volume-driven.

macro_indicators.reading: Continued decline for at least the next 12 months
macro_indicators.interpretation: Developer profit margins lead non-resi starts by about 18 months, which implies further square-footage declines.

risk_factors: Warehouse and parking starts continue to decline (-15% and -30% Y/Y in Sep square footage).
Bernstein's developer-margin model implies non-resi square-footage starts keep declining for at least the next 12 months.
Concentration of mega-project spending in data centers (about 30% of TTM) creates dependence on AI infrastructure spending.
Dollar value of starts is increasingly price inflation rather than volume.
Housing affordability is well below pre-pandemic levels, with possible further interest rate rises (Arkema section).
Breadth by value is 45%, below the historical median of 60%.

tension_points.bull_case: Sep non-resi square-footage decline slowed to about 5% from about 15% in Aug, and breadth of end markets with positive growth rose to about 70% from about 45%.
tension_points.bear_case: Developer profit margins lead starts by about 18 months and imply non-resi square-footage starts keep declining for at least 12 months. Warehouses and parking remain weak.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Non-resi square-footage starts turning positive Y/Y despite the developer-margin signal, or breadth by value staying below the historical median of 60%.
